The drag forces from the track and aerodynamics for that interval are calculated based on the starting speed. In most cases this required force is larger than what can be developed by the maximum propulsive force. This force is calculated by dividing the available power by the current speed and applying a constraint of a maximum force due to friction between the wheels and the track. The power provided by the battery locomotive is constrained by the available energy (state of charge) in the batteries. During the simulation, if the battery runs out of charge, it is no longer available as a power source until it can be recharged. The battery can be recharge with dynamic braking to remove energy from the consist or external charging at the end of the route [9]. The other two locomotives types are not limited by energy capacity during simulation and the total energy consumed over the route is integrated, providing a metrics for comparison including greenhouse gas emissions and cost of the fuel/energy source. Hybrid locomotives provide for a mix of power sources [10] and require a powering policy to determine how power should be sourced over the route. For most of the route, the power required to maintain the target speed does not require the maximum available power. As a result a powering policy is required to determine where to source the required power for the interval. A simple, a priori policy, termed “manual” or naïve policy, is used during this power requirements pass through the simulation. This policy simple sets a priority for the sources of available power. It does not consider costs or look ahead to power that may be needed further along the route. One option for an optimal look ahead powering policy is presented next. III. Optimal Powering Policy In this section we describe our initial optimal powering policy developed for SCORE. This policy minimizes the cost of energy while not violating the maximum power and stored battery energy constraints. The powering policy problem is treated as a linear program, with the decision variables being the power settings of the different locomotives for each interval.
